newsitem.title: UK: London marathon gets going amid tight security.
newsitem.headline: London marathon gets going amid tight security.

text.p: Thousands of runners set off from southeast London in the British capital's annual marathon on Sunday, amid concern that Irish guerrillas could try to sabotage the race.
Police said the start of the race had been free of any security scares, but they declined to comment on arrangements for policing the 26.2-mile (42.1 km) course.
"As with any event of this kind, we have been in close contact with the organisers and we have taken all appropriate steps," a police spokeswoman said.

The event's organisers said it was impossible to ensure that the race would not be disrupted. "Having an event that is held on public roads over 26.2 miles does mean that you cannot absolutely secure the whole of the course," Nick Bitel, the marathon's chief executive, said.

Hoax bomb warnings by the Irish Republican Army (IRA) forced the Grand National steeplechase, Britain's most popular horse race, to be abandoned less than an hour before the start on April 5, raising fears that the marathon could be the next event on the guerrillas' hitlist. The Grand National was rescheduled and run last Monday
More than 500,000 spectators were expected to watch the 27,000 runners as they followed the circuitous course that crosses the river Thames at Tower Bridge and finishes near Buckingham Palace.
The IRA, which is seeking an end to British rule of Northern Ireland, has stepped up activity to coincide with campaigning for Britain's May 1 general election.
The bomb hoaxes which disrupted the Grand National followed a campaign of real and false bomb warnings which have caused chaos on British motorways and railways over the past three weeks.

Nothern Ireland peace talks, from which the IRA's political wing have been been excluded, have been suspended during the British election campaign but had been bogged down over procedural difficulties for months.
